pages.text:
Turns Hydrogen Sulfide back into Sulfur, the way refineries do it (the Claus process): it burns the gas with Oxygen into Sulfur and water, which leaves as steam.
- 100 mB Hydrogen Sulfide and 50 mB Oxygen make a Sulfur Dust and 100 mB Steam in half a second, using 15 HU/t at 250°C or hotter.
- Hydrogen Sulfide in the top, Oxygen in the back, heat into the bottom. Sulfur Dust leaves by the left, Steam by the right; it pushes both out on its own.
- Speed Upgrades make it faster.
Oxygen comes from the Electrolyzer or the Air Separator. A bucket of Sour Crude Oil, distilled and both its sour cuts treated, gives about one Sulfur Dust.
